packageRules.description: A minor or patch update merges on green as a pull request into `ai/queue`, with no person in the loop; a major opens a pull request that waits for one. The rules below that hold, group or disable a package take it out of this default.

Every automerging minor and patch update is one group, so one branch and one CI run cover them rather than one per dependency on the shared runners. Each automerge is a pull request into `ai/queue` that merges once its own required checks pass. Later rules naming a `groupName` keep their own branch.

Nuxt 5 ships its fixes as nightly packages, so `nuxt` and the three `@nuxt/*` packages a module builds against are `npm:<name>-nightly@<tag>` aliases of a dist-tag: a lockfile refresh takes the newest nightly, and a nightly build is not a version Renovate can rank. Each name is matched beside its alias target. Replace the aliases with ranges and drop this rule once Nuxt 5 reaches `latest`.

`nitro` is pinned to one exact nightly build in the catalog and `overrides:`, not aliased to a dist-tag, so a lockfile refresh never moves it and a newer nightly is not proposed either. The pin holds for the two Nitro pull requests its `pnpm-workspace.yaml` comments link, which move Nitro's WebSocket upgrade listener and its Vite services. Drop this rule with the pin, back to a `^3` range, once both ship in a release.

`typescript` is aliased to `typescript-native-bridge` under `overrides:`, so a bump moves the bridge, the TypeScript behind it and `typescript-eslint` at once — a dedicated pass, never a routine update. A rule matches the resolved package name, so the alias target is named beside the alias.

`grapesjs` 0.23.7 was published without its JavaScript: the tarball ships `dist/index.d.ts` and no `grapes.mjs` or `grapes.min.js`, so it typechecks while every import of it fails to resolve, so it is pinned exactly to 0.23.6. Drop this rule and restore the catalog caret once a release ships its bundles again.

`vue-tsc` 3.3.12 reports `Property 'value' does not exist` on an imported ref used inside a template function (https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/issues/6237), so it is pinned exactly to 3.3.11. Drop this rule and restore the catalog caret once a release fixes the issue.

The pair is pinned to one exact RC and moves as one, following the `rc` dist-tag: drizzle publishes a per-commit build (`1.0.0-rc.5-ab785fc`) under a tag per branch, and without the tag every one of those is a proposal. A release candidate can change what `db:gen` emits, so the grouped bump is read rather than merged on green. Drop `followTag` once 1.0.0 reaches `latest`.

`.node-version` is the one node pin, and `@types/node` follows its major with its own minors lagging node's, so the two move in one branch. Renovate's `node` versioning calls a major stable only once its LTS date has passed and an odd major never, so under the default unstable filter the pin could reach no major past its own; the repo tracks the Current line, which is what `pnpm update:node` writes too, so unstable is not ignored here. A major still opens a PR for a person.

A plugin's `engines.node` floor follows the pin, as `pnpm update:node` writes it. Renovate's default range strategy leaves a `>=` range the new version already satisfies, so the floor is bumped in the node branch beside `.node-version`.

pnpm ships its new workspace settings in minors (`autoDedupe` arrived in 12.6), and a setting this repo should turn on is visible only in the release notes, never in a green check. So the bot never merges a pnpm bump: each one is taken by the hand pass, which reads each release it crosses with `gh release view` and lands the settings worth taking in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` in the same commit, and the bot's PR for it is closed as superseded. Its own group keeps that read-before-merge bump out of the automerging non-major branch.
The collector calls its own reusable workflow at `@ai/queue`; a branch ref is not a version to bump, and a tag here would freeze the collector on one release.

A Docker digest moving under its tag is the publisher's routine rebuild — a patched base image republished under the same tag, versioned or not — so it lands on the same branch automerge the minor/patch rule above gives everything else. An action's digest is left out on purpose: an action ships a fix as a new tag, so a digest that moves under the same version is a re-pointed tag — the shape a SHA pin exists to catch — and it opens a PR for a person.
